title: Define SCM v1 schema + example payloads + validation rules
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
## Context
Console (cost breakdown/transparency) + Optimize (what-if scenario sweeps) need a canonical, versioned schema for inference cost estimation/attribution so we can deliver consistent output across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

This ticket defines:
1) SCM v1 request/response schema (protobuf + JSON shape)
2) Required vs optional inputs + semantics/units
3) Example payloads for common workloads
4) Validation rules + error mapping requirements (client-safe)

References:
- Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/standard-cost-model-api-prd.json
- SCM spec v1: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/standard-cost-model-spec-v1.json
- API conventions: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/cost-model-api-conventions.json
- ADR-0147 versioning: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0147-cost-model-versioning-and-negotiation.json

## Goals
- Produce a concrete SCM v1 contract that Cost Model service, Console, and Optimize can implement without ambiguity.
- Ensure determinism: same inputs => same outputs (within v1), independent of deployment mode.
- Explicit assumptions + confidence semantics so missing telemetry can be represented without silent guesswork.
- Guardrails: validation + stable field naming to reduce churn.

## Non-goals
- Pricing/discounts/contract terms (handled separately; SCM is technical cost attribution).
- Customer billing/invoice source of truth.

## Proposed schema (SCM v1)
### Top-level request (EstimateRequest)
Required:
- scm_version: string ("1" for v1)
- request_id: string (idempotency + audit correlation; client supplied)
- mode: enum { ESTIMATE, EXPLAIN } (NOTE: both return breakdown; EXPLAIN adds contributing_factors)
- model: object-ish fields flattened in proto
  - model_id: string (catalog id)
  - model_revision: string (optional, but recommended; if absent -> assumption logged)
- deployment_context:
  - deployment_type: enum { HOSTED, DEDICATED, PRIVATE }
  - region: string (required for determinism; can be "unknown" only for offline tooling)
  - gpu_sku: string (required unless model_id maps deterministically to single sku; otherwise validation error)
- workload:
  - tokens_input: int64 (>=0)
  - tokens_output: int64 (>=0)
  - request_count: int32 (>=1; default=1)

Optional (but strongly recommended for accuracy/confidence):
- runtime_signals:
  - prefill_ms: double (>=0)
  - decode_ms: double (>=0)
  - batch_size_effective: double (>=1.0)
  - kv_cache_hit_rate: double (0..1)
  - kv_cache_type: enum { NONE, PREFIX, KV, OTHER } (v1: NONE|KV; reserve others)
- optimization_profile:
  - quant_profile_id: string ("fp16_default", "int8_w8a8", etc.)
  - batching_enabled: bool
  - caching_enabled: bool

### Top-level response (CostResponse)
Required:
- scm_version: string
- request_id: string
- currency: string ("USD" for v1; contractually fixed)
- total_cost_usd: double (>=0)
- breakdown_cost_usd: repeated component entries (sum must equal total within epsilon)
- assumptions: repeated strings (human-readable, stable codes included)
- confidence:
  - confidence_level: enum { HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW }
  - confidence_score: double (0..1) (heuristic, deterministic)

For EXPLAIN mode only:
- contributing_factors: repeated strings (e.g., "low kv_cache_hit_rate", "batch_size_effective<2")

### Cost components (breakdown)
v1 components (stable ids):
- compute_prefill_usd
- compute_decode_usd
- memory_kv_cache_usd
- overhead_control_plane_usd (bounded, usually small; can be 0)
- amortized_warmup_usd (optional; only when explicitly modeled)

Component rules:
- Each component includes: component_id (string), cost_usd (double), percent_of_total (double 0..1), notes (string optional)
- If a component is not applicable, omit it (don’t send 0 unless there’s a meaningful semantic distinction).

## Validation rules (v1)
Hard errors (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT):
- Missing required fields: request_id, scm_version, mode, model_id, deployment_type, region (unless explicitly offline), tokens_input/tokens_output
- Negative token counts or request_count < 1
- kv_cache_hit_rate outside [0,1]
- batch_size_effective < 1
- Unsupported scm_version per negotiation rules (see ENG-23203)

Soft validation (200 with assumptions + reduced confidence):
- model_revision missing -> assumption "ASSUMPTION_MODEL_REVISION_UNPINNED"
- runtime_signals missing -> assumptions added; confidence lowered to MEDIUM/LOW depending on which fields absent
- quant_profile_id missing -> assumption "ASSUMPTION_QUANT_PROFILE_DEFAULTED"

Determinism requirements:
- Confidence scoring must be a pure function of request inputs (no external time-varying lookups beyond versioned tables).
- Breakdown ordering must be deterministic (sort by component_id).

## Example payloads to include (in schema package)
1) Hosted chat completion, warm cache, batching on
2) Dedicated batch job, cold cache, high output tokens
3) Private/VPC with missing runtime signals (estimate-only; low confidence)
4) Error example: missing region + missing gpu_sku

These examples must be checked in as fixtures and used by:
- Docs (Console tooltips)
- Integration tests (Console + Optimize staging)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] SCM v1 schema definitions committed (proto + JSON mapping notes) with stable field names.
- [x] Example request/response fixtures exist for at least the 3 primary deployment types.
- [x] Validation rules documented + implemented in shared helpers (client/server).
- [x] Explicit assumptions + confidence semantics included and consistent with the v1 spec.
- [x] Review checklist completed (below) and sign-off from Platform + Console + Optimize.

## Review checklist
API + contract:
- [x] Field naming follows API conventions; no ambiguous units.
- [x] Required fields are truly required for determinism.
- [x] Backward/forward compatibility strategy documented (ADR-0147).

Console needs:
- [x] Breakdown component ids map to stable UI sections.
- [x] Assumptions and confidence can be rendered without additional interpretation.

Optimize needs:
- [x] Request allows injecting hypothetical batching/caching/quant candidates.
- [x] Response includes enough structure to compare deltas across scenarios.

Runtime + telemetry:
- [x] runtime_signals fields match runtime metric naming/tags.
- [x] Missing signals behave predictably (assumptions + low confidence).

Testing:
- [x] Golden JSON fixtures + schema validation tests exist.
- [x] Deterministic serialization (component ordering, rounding policy specified).

## Implementation notes / where this lands
- Target repo change: shared types package used by cost-model-service + Console backend + Optimize.
- Add JSON fixtures under /testdata/scm/v1/.
- Add validators: validateEstimateRequestV1(), validateExplainRequestV1().
- Add a small "schema README" documenting units + rounding (USD to 1e-6 in service; clients should display with currency formatting).

## Open questions
- Do we treat "region=unknown" as allowed for internal offline tools only? Proposed: allow only when a header "X-Redwood-Internal: true" is present; otherwise 400.
- Do we want to include "energy" as a component in v1? Proposed: no; leave for v2.

## Status updates
- 2025-02-03 (Jordan Lee): Drafted proto fields + component taxonomy; circulated to Dylan/Chloe (Console) + Hassan (Optimize) for feedback on component ids and assumptions.
- 2025-02-06 (Jordan Lee): Added example fixtures for Hosted/Dedicated/Private; aligned confidence semantics with PM guidance (Console copy uses "Estimated" + "Low confidence").
- 2025-02-11 (Jordan Lee): Implemented validators + deterministic ordering; added negative tests for missing region/gpu_sku + invalid kv_cache_hit_rate.
- 2025-02-18 (Jordan Lee): Merged PR-18421; unblocked service skeleton + client integrations. Remaining: version negotiation ticket (ENG-23203) + end-to-end staging integration tests (tracked elsewhere).
comments: Marissa Cole (2025-02-05): Please keep breakdown component ids stable and human-readable; Console will use them as section keys. Also need assumptions to be both machine-stable and user-presentable (code + friendly copy).

Dylan Brooks (2025-02-05): +1 on stable ids. For UI we also need ordering; deterministic sort by component_id works. Please ensure percent_of_total sums to 1.0 within tolerance so we don’t show confusing rounding drift.

Hassan Mirza (2025-02-06): Optimize will run multi-scenario sweeps; request_count is useful but we also need to override batching/caching/quant per scenario. Current optional optimization_profile is sufficient for v1; we’ll batch requests client-side for now.

Logan Wright (2025-02-07): runtime_signals naming should match emitted tags; avoid adding high-cardinality fields in schema (no per-request GPU id). batch_size_effective as double is good since it’s a derived metric.

Priya Natarajan (2025-02-12): Make sure determinism language is explicit: no dynamic pricing tables in v1 response; only versioned cost coefficients. Also call out validation behavior (hard vs soft) clearly so clients implement safe fallbacks.
